SEC-005's Fix would wrap outbound gateway calls with require_safe_url(); SEC-001's Fix would encrypt the gateway credentials. payment_engine.py:3391-3395 currently attaches the (plaintext) secret_key as an `Authorization: Bearer` header to an admin-supplied target_url with follow_redirects=True. coverage_gaps: NEW FINDING, P1, NOT IN ANY PACKET RECORD - Law 37 rate limiting is effectively fail-closed BY ACCIDENT and will deny ALL traffic whenever Valkey is unreachable. Chain verified empirically: infrastructure/valkey/client.py:159-167 returns _NoOpValkey after 3 retries; rate_limit_middleware.py:98-101 caches it in self._redis permanently; :148 `if redis is not None` is True because _NoOpValkey is not None; client.py:93-102 _NoOpValkeyPipeline.execute() returns []; rate_limit_middleware.py:158 `results[1]` raises IndexError; the broad `except Exception` at :170-176 converts it to HTTP 429 'Rate limiting unavailable'. I reproduced every step: valkey_client() -> _NoOpValkey, pipeline -> len 0, results[1] -> IndexError. Consequences: (a) the intended in-memory allow-path at :178-188 is unreachable dead code; (b) self._redis is cached at :96 so Valkey is never retried for the process lifetime; (c) the module docstring at client.py:9-10 claims 'graceful no-op otherwise', which is the opposite of observed behaviour. This is a self-inflicted outage risk, not merely an absent control - recommend P1. No record in packets/18_security.json covers it (SEC-012 only covers the default-off flag).

NEW FINDING, P1, NOT IN ANY PACKET RECORD - Law 282/Law 58 PII leak on every login, CONFIRMING T13. domains/accounts/services/auth/auth_service.py:2063-2064 prints user.id and user.email to stderr on every successful login, with a function-local `import sys` at :2063. Running setup_structlog() then print(...file=sys.stderr) emitted the address verbatim, while the same value passed through structlog came out as {"email": "[REDACTED]"}. So the email is NOT redacted.
